images.note: Beat 1 (new immigration wave): Augustus F. Sherman's Ellis Island administrative portrait of a Ruthenian (Carpatho-Rusyn) woman, ca. 1906 — a southern/eastern-European newcomer of the post-1880 wave. Contemporary photograph. Alt: NYPL's companion 'Italian woman' (digital ID 418055) also verified at 1600px but is the same institution; Lewis Hine's Ellis Island prints at the Met have no published API images; LOC derivatives cap at ~1024px. No qualifying second-institution alt.

images.title: Ruthenian woman — Ellis Island portrait by Augustus F. Sherman, ca. 1906

images.note: Beat 3 (Chinese Exclusion Act backstory): 'The Chinese had come for the railroads and the gold country, thousands of workers.' Primary is Alfred A. Hart's ca. 1863–1869 Central Pacific construction photo (Alfred A. Hart Photograph Collection, Stanford University, via NPR) — visually confirmed: Chinese workers breaking rock in the Sierra Nevada, one in a conical straw hat. Alt shows Watkins's 1877 trestle with Chinese workers on it; weaker source chain (blog CDN) documented honestly.
images.source: NPR/KACU (Alfred A. Hart Photograph Collection, Stanford University)

images.note: Beat 2 (immigrant city): the book's halftone of Riis's 1888 Mulberry Bend photograph — the exact tenement image the script invokes ('Fifth Avenue mansions against tenement blocks'). From the 1890 first edition of How the Other Half Lives. Alt: Museum of the City of New York's Riis collection unreachable; LOC derivatives of Riis photos cap at ~1024px. No qualifying second-institution alt.
images.source: Internet Archive (How the Other Half Lives, 1890 first edition scan)
images.title: 'Bandits' Roost' — halftone from How the Other Half Lives, 1890

images.note: Beat 3 (Angel Island, 1910; 'Ellis processed; Angel detained'): carved Chinese characters visible on the detention barracks wall — the poems the script names ('poems carved into the wood'). Later photograph (2013) of the surviving historic wall, documented as a contemporary photo of the period artifact. Alt: NPS 1996 Jim Burke nomination photos not available as individual assets; AIISF Poetry Finder is JS-only with no extractable image URLs; history.com's poem-wall photo is Getty-licensed. No qualifying second-institution alt.
images.source: Library of Congress (Carol M. Highsmith Archive, 2013)
images.title: Carved Chinese poetry on the Angel Island detention barracks wall

images.note: Beat 3 (Chinese Exclusion Act, 1882): front-page wood engraving 'THE ONLY ONE BARRED OUT' showing a Chinese man barred from the 'Golden Gate of Liberty' — published April 1, 1882, one month before the Act's May 6, 1882 signing; the first race-based federal ban. Located via djvu word search on the issue's OCR. Alt: LOC's copy of this engraving maxes at 749x1024; Rutgers RUcore copy 552x600; WSU Omeka item timed out. No qualifying second-institution alt.
images.source: Internet Archive (Frank Leslie's Illustrated Newspaper, April 1, 1882)
images.title: 'The Only One Barred Out' — Frank Leslie's Illustrated Newspaper, April 1, 1882

images.note: Beat 3 ('two laws, one year'): CHAP. 376, approved August 3, 1882, 'An act to regulate Immigration' — 'a duty of fifty cents for each and every passenger not a citizen of the United States,' barring convicts, the mentally ill, and anyone likely to become a public charge. Primary legal text, Statutes at Large vol. 22 p. 214 (scan leaf n243, found via OCR search for the fifty-cent clause). Alt: GovInfo offers only full-volume PDFs; no second >=1200px page-image source found.
images.source: Internet Archive (U.S. Statutes at Large, 1881–1883, vol. 22)
images.title: Immigration Act of 1882, Chap. 376 — Statutes at Large, vol. 22, p. 214

images.note: Beat 4 (Immigration Restriction League, 1894; literacy test): Senator Henry Cabot Lodge (1850–1924), who carried the literacy test in Congress. Bain News Service portrait, visually confirmed (bearded senator, Bain stamp, signature). Alt: Sargent's 1890 NPG portrait only available at 535px via Sartle; LOC's Harris & Ewing Lodge photo (1922) caps at 1024x793. No qualifying second-institution alt.
images.title: Senator Henry Cabot Lodge — Bain News Service portrait

images.note: Beat 4 ('race suicide' / 'inferior races'): title page of Madison Grant's The Passing of the Great Race. Alt: other scans of the work are same-institution (Internet Archive); no second-institution >=1200px source found.
